text:
frank: heads up — we had a customer onboarding failure this morning (tenant: solara). SCIM create got a 409 while our audit index shows no user.create for that window (2026-03-25T03:46Z). KMS logs show Decrypt denied.

neha: which principal got denied? paste the tiny log snippet if you have it.

frank: proc logs:
```
2026-03-25T03:45:58Z INFO provisioner: start create externalId=solara-914
2026-03-25T03:46:00Z ERROR audit-publisher.kms: Decrypt AccessDenied on CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555555:key/aa11-bb22
2026-03-25T03:46:00Z ERROR audit-publisher: publish failed -> DLQ
2026-03-25T03:46:01Z ERROR scim-client: HTTP 409 {"detail":"User with externalId already exists"}
```

carmen: likely role rotation or grant stale. Did we rotate the audit publisher role or change the key policy recently?

frank: We rotated a bunch of provisioning roles during the maintenance window last night. I thought the rotation script would recreate grants but apparently one service missed.

neha: quick triage checklist: 1) run `aws sts get-caller-identity` from the publisher pod; 2) `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key>`; 3) CloudTrail filter for KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied at timestamp. That'll show the role ARN and the error.

carmen: also check whether the CMK key policy was changed to remove iam:Decrypt for the account principals. Sometimes a policy tighten removes previously implicit access.

frank: running checks now — list-grants shows grants for `role/provisioner-v1` and `role/ingest-worker` but not `role/audit-publisher-rotated`. sts shows the publisher pod is now running as `arn:aws:iam::555555:role/audit-publisher-rotated`. so grant missing.

neha: that matches. immediate mitigation: create a grant for the new role with Operations ["Decrypt","GenerateDataKey"]. Prefer creating grants before you flip the role in rotation.

carmen: agreed. long-term: key policy should reference a stable provisioning principal (role alias) instead of ad-hoc grants, or our rotation runbook should create the new grant pre-cutover. Add test `aws kms decrypt` as a smoke step in rotation pipeline.

frank: created grant, retried the onboarding call: SCIM returns 201 now for test user. replayed DLQ for the 03:44-03:48 window and re-emitted audit.create rows.

neha: good. two operational items from this: 1) we had no alert for spikes in KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied for audit-publisher — add an alert. 2) our audit indexer treats decryption failures as DLQ-only; we should surface counts in the console per-tenant so customer-facing incidents are easier to correlate.

carmen: also note a contributing factor: the customer's SAML assertion was using transient NameID for some logins. That can cause our provisioning to attempt duplicate creates because we link externalId to NameID when present. We should reject provisioning flows that present transient NameID for onboarding (or ask customer to use persistent).

frank: customer said they rotated their IdP cert last week and temporarily started issuing transient NameIDs for certain flows; they blamed a vendor default. I've asked them to switch back to persistent for provisioning endpoints.

neha: add to postmortem: root cause = audit-publisher role rotation without pre-created KMS grant; contributing = transient NameID from IdP causing duplicate create attempts; operational gap = missing KMS AccessDenied alert for audit-publisher.

carmen: remediation checklist I will file: - pre-rotation script to create grants then switch role - rotation smoke-test `aws kms decrypt` step - add alert for KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied spikes for audit-publisher - reject transient NameID in onboarding handshake and return clear error to the integrator - run DLQ replay and reconciliation job for the tenant.

ops-bot: DLQ replay job started (job id dlq-rpl-20260325-01) for audit.topic targeting tenant=solara.

frank: DLQ replay completed, audit rows restored, no new 409s in 45m. closing this thread unless anyone objects. thanks all :rocket:

security-bot: flagged: open RFC to update rotation runbook and alerting (ticket SEC-2026-314).
